parts.name: Left finger — Generalist yellow, mirror of the right
Left handle-gear — black, the left handle: one print with its gear (both hooks, two strap-loop slots, tail fused into the hub), turns on the base’s left post
Right handle-gear — black, the right handle: one print with its gear (both hooks, two strap-loop slots, tail fused into the hub), driven by the pinion, turns on the right post
Pinion — black, centred, full-height teeth, 4 countersunk M3 into the STS3215’s horn
Base — black flat plate with a pivot post for each handle-gear; bears on the STS3215’s rails, 4 M2 into its case, a window over its hump; a wrist tab below the servo takes the wrist bracket (2 M3)

Top plate — black, over the handle-gears and fingers on 2 corner pillars (none between the fingers); a C-shaped ring round each pivot runs in its handle-gear’s groove, so each axle is held top and bottom

Wrist bracket — black L: its leg clamps flat under the base’s wrist tab (2 M3, beside the STS3215, not on it), its foot lies across the arm’s J6 axis and takes the tool plate; a zip-tie point for the servo’s bus cable
Tool plate — the gripper’s side of the wrist interface (twin of Seeed’s Connector B): 4 M3 up into the bracket, slips over the hub, 3 radial M3
Wrist hub (SO-101) — stays on the arm: 4 countersunk M3 into the wrist-roll STS3215’s horn, in place of the stock fixed jaw; Mount 1’s hub outside, so every Mount 1 tool plate slips over it
Motor — Feetech STS3215 (the SO-101 servo), reference only (not printed): read back-driven as the grip encoder
SO-101 Arm (printed) — reference, The Robot Studio’s URDF and meshes (SO-ARM100, Apache-2.0), stock gripper removed
SO-101 Arm (sts3215) — reference, The Robot Studio’s URDF and meshes (SO-ARM100, Apache-2.0), stock gripper removed
